description: While building the git-gate PreToolUse redirect, the first implementation passed the full tool_input object (including description and other fields) as updatedInput. This build silently ignored it and ran the original command instead, so a raw git write executed with no rewrite and no audit entry, with no error surfaced anywhere. Verified empirically both ways via a live git-version probe: stdout JSON decisions (deny) are honored, and updatedInput with ONLY the changed field ({"command": ...}) is applied; the full-object shape is not.
correction: updatedInput must carry only the changed fields, exactly matching the documented example shape ({"command": ...}). Fixed in .claude/hooks/git-gate.py with the empirical note inline; regression-cased in .claude/hooks/tests/test_git_gate.py.
systemic_fix: git-gate.py emits minimal-shape updatedInput with the empirical finding documented inline and a test asserting the exact shape. Secondary finding recorded in skills/git/SKILL.md: hook script edits on this OneDrive/FUSE mount can take a turn (sometimes several calls) to propagate to the hook process, so gate changes must be probed with a harmless classified command before relying on them.
